final_candidates.decision_summary: Conservative hydrophobic substitution with strong MSA and PLM support; likely improves core packing and stability without disrupting function.
Highly plausible by PLM and conservative in nature; despite lower MSA frequency, it may stabilize the core with minimal perturbation.
Reasonable MSA support and solid structure compatibility; conservative hydrophobic change likely preserves local packing and overall stability.

stop_reason.detail: Additional evidence is unlikely to change the top-3 given strong support for the leading candidates and the limited applicability of remaining tools.

history.rationale: Conservative expansion of a hydrophobic residue may fill a buried pocket in the HA1 globular domain, improving core packing. It avoids the receptor-binding loops and conserved cysteines.
No new evidence; retaining candidate based on general stability rationale.
Weak but positive structure score and low evolutionary/MSA support; retained below more supported candidates.
Conservative hydrophobic substitution with increased buried volume may stabilize the HA1 fold. It lies outside the receptor-binding surface and the fusion peptide.
No new evidence; retaining candidate with minor hydrophobic change.
Reasonable MSA support (0.144) and solid structure compatibility (0.494); conservative hydrophobic change likely preserves packing.
Replacing an oxidizable methionine with leucine reduces heat-induced damage while preserving hydrophobic character. This position is not part of the receptor-binding site.
No new evidence; retaining candidate that may improve core stability.
Strongest support from both MSA (0.358) and PLM (1.0); conservative hydrophobic substitution likely beneficial for core packing and stability.
A larger beta-branched residue in the HA2 stem helix may improve trimer core packing and thermostability. This site is distal to both receptor binding and the fusion peptide.
No new evidence available; retaining conservative hydrophobic substitution that may improve folding stability.
Zero MSA frequency and negligible PLM score; no structural context, so it lacks any meaningful support for stability.

rejection.reason: Zero MSA frequency and negligible PLM score; no structural context, so it lacks any meaningful support for stability.

history.rationale: Reducing mainchain entropy with glycine-to-alanine may increase local stability in the HA1 domain. It is near the cleavage-site base but does not directly disrupt the polybasic site.
No new evidence; retaining candidate with small to larger hydrophobic residue.
High evolutionary support (0.33) but weak PLM and structure scores reduce confidence; still a plausible conservative change.

Removing an oxidation-prone methionine in the HA2 coiled-coil region may improve stability during heat exposure. Isoleucine provides similar steric packing but with higher resistance to oxidative damage.
No new evidence; retaining candidate with plausible hydrophobic stabilization.
PLM score is maximal (1.0) indicating high sequence plausibility; despite low MSA frequency, the mutation is conservative and could stabilize the core.
Conservative valine-to-isoleucine substitution adds a methyl group that can improve hydrophobic packing in the HA2 stem. This is a minimal perturbation away from functional sites.
No new evidence; retaining candidate that may add hydrophobic packing.
Marginal MSA and PLM scores, no structure; remains a low-confidence backup.

Leucine-to-isoleucine in the HA2 helix may enhance core packing while maintaining hydrophobic character. The mutation is in a structurally supporting region rather than the membrane-proximal fusion machinery.
No new evidence; retaining candidate with similar hydrophobic substitution.
No MSA frequency and very low PLM; insufficient evidence to justify further consideration.

rejection.reason: No MSA frequency and very low PLM; insufficient evidence to justify further consideration.

history.rationale: Adding a methyl group in the HA2 helix may fill a small cavity and stabilize the prefusion conformation. It preserves the local charged and polar residues involved in trimer contacts.
No new evidence; retaining candidate with possible packing improvement.
Moderate MSA support (0.135) but low PLM; retains some promise as a conservative aliphatic substitution.
Conservative isoleucine substitution may improve hydrophobic packing in the N-terminal HA1 subdomain. It is well outside the receptor-binding domain and should preserve cell-entry function.
No new evidence; retaining candidate as plausible but lower confidence.
Best structure compatibility (0.508) but lacks MSA/PLM support; kept as a lower-confidence candidate given structure signal.
